cells.tense: The perceiving is full and steady, and you are here with the pen.
cells.act: put the frame on the table before anyone asks
cells.ask: Once this week, before anyone asks you to explain, say plainly what shape you see in the matter at hand — just the frame, one sentence, no defense. Say it and stop.
cells.core:
You take in the whole picture at once — several things true at the same time, none of them wrong. That isn't confusion. It's perception full enough to hold what other people have to take turns holding. You can sit with two people who are dead certain of opposite things and not pick a side to keep the peace; you name what each one is standing on, and where they meet. Nobody has to lose. The light pulling you is that one — not being right, being able to say what's so.

So this week, say the shape first. One place where you'd normally wait to be included before saying anything. Put the frame on the table — what you see, plain, once. Not proved, not argued. Offered while it's still alive among you. You'll find out quickly who was waiting for it.
cells.sheetLine: You can say what's so before it's argued.
cells.verb: Holding many truths at once, in full view
cells.place: Facing the light you're drawn toward, not yet arrived

cells.tense: But you've already left the room for one that hasn't happened yet.
cells.act: face one way for three days
cells.ask: Name one direction you actually want to head in — one, not a list — and hold it for three days. When other pulls come, leave them unexamined and keep going this way.
cells.core:
You take in so much that you start bracing for the future in every direction at once — checking each version of what might come, keeping every possible reading open in case one turns out to be the live one. That stays generous in your head. Out here, nobody can tell which light you're following, and neither can you. Checking starts standing in for going.

Name one direction. Not the best one, the truest one — the thing you actually want, not the thing that makes the most sense. Then face it, and leave the other directions unexamined for three days. You'll feel the pull to keep scanning; that's just habit. A heading settles most of it without any further work. Radiance shows up once something has been carried all the way through, not while it's still being sized up.

cells.tense: Nothing new has caught your eye for a while now — you keep going back through a door you already closed.
cells.act: join someone in the work so the two streams run as one
cells.ask: Take something you'd normally read by yourself and read it alongside another person, saying what you notice as you go. Not a report afterward — out loud, as it lands.
cells.core:
You can still perceive, but nothing ahead is lighting you up. What you want doesn't pull; you can list it and feel nothing. So you stand at a closed door rereading it, as if the next bright thing has to start there. It doesn't. A pull toward something has to move between two people before you'll trust it as yours.

So don't try to want harder. Take something you'd normally read by yourself and read it beside another person — saying what you notice as you notice it, not a summary when you're done. Two streams running together is what tells you the pull is real. One of them speaking a direction out loud is enough to start the water again; the charge comes from beside you, not from you pushing on the place that's gone quiet.
cells.sheetLine: What draws you needs a second person nearby to be believed.

cells.tense: What you perceive keeps landing among people, and the credit for it is left lying there.
cells.act: act on the private sense of what is right
cells.ask: Wherever you see something unfair — small or large — do the thing you know is right instead of naming it, and afterward don't tell anyone you did, including by the way you look.
cells.core:
You know which way is fair before it's said, and you move on it — adjust the thing, make it right, cover the gap — and if someone asked you after, you'd say you just did what anyone would. It isn't nothing. You're moving by what's right, a hundred small calls a day, and you file it under circumstance.

The constancy is yours. So take the next case where you feel the small wrongness and act on it without announcing the act, without explaining it, without taking credit for facing it. Then, privately, count it as a call you made rather than something that happened to pass through you. The compass you trust is the same one you keep leaving unnamed. That's why so few feel sure of it — including you.
cells.sheetLine: You steer by fairness and call it circumstance.

attempts.check: The record calls the signature 'Bound' — a capacity through a channel, seen in one part of a life — and its parent is Wisdom. My draft must not claim the person's history, what Knowing has cost, or that they are in fact right and others wrong; the reader could reasonably say 'it's not abundance, it's just noise.' The ask survives my read being wrong: if Knowing is not the issue, tracing the frame still shows something usable. The sentence that serves me most is the one that would make others' blindness the villain — I removed it; what serves the person is only that what they see has a shape they can offer without arguing anyone into it.
